passage: I'm Darshan, and my little brother Suraj is five. At our cousin's birthday he spent the first half hour behind Amma's legs, holding her dupatta. When Mami asked his name, he whispered it into Amma's side. An uncle snapped, "Say hello properly, don't be like that," and Suraj went stiff, eyes down. Amma just said, "He'll come when he's ready." He watched musical chairs for three rounds. He let go and stood near the edge. In the fourth round he was in it, laughing. I can't know what he was thinking, but I think he wanted to play all along.

qa.q: Where did Suraj spend the first half hour?
qa.a: Behind Amma's legs, holding her dupatta.

qa.q: What does Darshan think Suraj wanted all along?
qa.a: Darshan thinks Suraj was shy but wanted to play all along, even while hiding behind Amma and watching.

qa.q: Which response helped Suraj more, the uncle's or Amma's, and why?
qa.a: Amma's; letting him come when ready gave him time, while the uncle's push made him freeze.

qa.q: How might the uncle see Suraj after the fourth round?
qa.a: He may realise Suraj wasn't being rude, just needing time, since he ended up laughing in the game.

grounding: An older brother watches a five-year-old hide at a party, freeze when pushed to say hello, and join only after watching.

passage:
Monday. At the new playgroup, four-year-old Lakshmi stood pressed against her father's knees. When the teacher asked her name, she whispered "Lakshmi" into Thomas's shirt. Thomas didn't push. They sat on the bench and watched the sand tray.
Wednesday. Lakshmi let go of his hand to stand near the sand tray. A boy offered her a spade and she shook her head, but she kept watching him.
Friday. Lakshmi took the spade. By the end of the morning she was filling buckets beside the same boy, humming. At home she told her father, "He's my friend. His name is Omar."

qa.q: What did the boy offer Lakshmi on Wednesday?
qa.a: He offered her a spade.

qa.q: What does Lakshmi watching the boy after shaking her head suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: She seems curious and wanted to join in, but was still too shy to be ready yet.

qa.q: What choice did Thomas make on Monday, and how did it help?
qa.a: He didn't push; they sat and watched, which gave Lakshmi time to warm up over the week.

qa.q: How might Omar feel when Lakshmi finally takes the spade?
qa.a: He may feel pleased that his patient offer was accepted and that he has a new friend.

grounding: Over one week, a slow-to-warm four-year-old whispers, watches and finally joins play because her father gives her time.

passage: Rain had pushed Ishita's birthday party indoors, and twenty children were squeezed into one small living room. Maria stood behind her mother's legs, holding the gift. 'Say hello to Ishita, beta! Don't be shy!' an aunty said loudly. Maria pressed her face into the back of Mama's knee and went still. 'She'll come when she's ready,' Mama said, and sat on the sofa, letting Maria lean. Maria watched the block tower grow for a long time. Then she walked over, held out the gift and whispered, 'Happy birthday.' Ishita beamed. 'Want to build?' Maria nodded and knelt beside her.

qa.q: Why was the party indoors?
qa.a: Rain had pushed it indoors.

qa.q: What was Maria feeling when the aunty told her to say hello?
qa.a: She felt shy and overwhelmed, freezing with her face pressed into Mama's knee.

qa.q: What did Mama do that helped Maria join in?
qa.a: She didn't push; she sat down, let Maria lean and watch, and said she'd come when she was ready.

qa.q: How might Ishita feel when Maria whispers 'Happy birthday'?
qa.a: Ishita is pleased and welcoming, beaming and inviting Maria to build.

grounding: Shows a young child who hides behind a parent at a crowded party, freezes when pushed to say hello, and joins after watching.

passage: At the colony's Diwali get-together, Mohit held on to the back of Papa's kurta. When Mrs. Kapoor bent down and asked his name, he whispered it into Papa's sleeve. 'Go, play with the boys!' Dadi said, giving him a little push. Mohit went stiff and started to cry. Papa picked him up. 'Let's just watch for a bit.' From Papa's arms, Mohit watched Jomon and three others rolling marbles along chalk lines. Then he tapped Papa's shoulder. 'Down.' He crouched at the edge of the game. Jomon slid a blue marble toward him without a word.

qa.q: What were Jomon and the others doing?
qa.a: Rolling marbles along chalk lines.

qa.q: Why did Mohit go stiff and cry when Dadi pushed him?
qa.a: Being pushed made him frightened and more frozen, because he needs time before joining.

qa.q: What did Papa do differently from Dadi?
qa.a: He picked Mohit up and let him watch for a while, so Mohit could choose when to join.

qa.q: How might Jomon see Mohit crouching at the edge?
qa.a: Jomon seems friendly and easygoing, sliding a marble over without making a fuss.

grounding: Shows a young child who whispers answers, freezes when pushed to play, and joins only after being allowed to watch.

passage:
'Papa, do I have to say hello to everyone at the wedding?'
'Who told you that?'
'Masi. Last time.' Kishore pulled at his sherwani button. 'My tummy went hard.'
Vikas sat on the bed. 'You don't have to. You can stand with me and watch first.'
'And then?'
'Then, if you want, you can wave. Or show someone your car.'
At the wedding Kishore stood behind Vikas, watching the cousins race round the chairs. Then he tugged his hand. 'Papa. Can I show Guddu my car?'
'Go on.'
He went, slowly, holding the car out like a ticket.

qa.q: What did Kishore want to show Guddu?
qa.a: His car.

qa.q: What does Kishore's 'My tummy went hard' show?
qa.a: He felt nervous and scared when he was pushed to say hello to everyone.

qa.q: Why did Vikas's plan help?
qa.a: It let Kishore watch first and choose his own small step, like showing his car, instead of forcing hellos.

qa.q: How might Masi's 'say hello to everyone' have felt to Kishore?
qa.a: It made Kishore feel pressured and frozen, which is why he still remembered it with worry.

grounding: Shows a young child who wants to join in but needs time, and a parent who lets him watch first rather than pushing him to say hello.

passage:
Playgroup teacher's note, after Mishti's birthday party.
Kashish arrived holding her mother Seema's dupatta and stayed behind her legs. An aunty bent down: "Say hello! Don't be shy!" Kashish pressed her face into the dupatta and went completely still.
I asked the aunty to give her time. Seema sat on the floor near the blocks, and Kashish sat on her lap, watching the others build.
After a long while she whispered to me, "Can I put the red one?" I nodded. By cake time she was building next to Mishti, still quiet.
Next week in class I will seat her near the block corner, and let her join when she is ready.

qa.q: What was Kashish holding when she arrived?
qa.a: Her mother Seema's dupatta.

qa.q: How did Kashish feel when the aunty told her to say hello?
qa.a: She felt shy and frozen; she pressed her face into the dupatta and went completely still.

qa.q: What helped Kashish join in, according to the teacher's note?
qa.a: Being given time, sitting on Seema's lap near the blocks to watch first, and a simple nod when she whispered to join.

qa.q: How might the aunty see Kashish's silence, and what would change if she waited?
qa.a: The aunty may think Kashish is being rude or just shy; if she waited, Kashish could warm up at her own pace instead of freezing.

grounding: Shows a slow-to-warm child who hides behind her mother, whispers, and joins play after watching, and how pushing to say hello deepens the freeze.
